title: The DISTIL sources file
description: workareas/<workarea>/sources.json: what a DISTIL run is for and what it reads. The main session writes it at intake and edits it to fold in a new source or a ruling; the distil workflow reads it, and `tim distil status` turns it into the workflow's work list. `tim distil` checks what a schema cannot: source ids and file slugs are unique, every precedence entry names a source and every source is ranked, and every repo in `repos` is also a `repo:<key>` source.

programme.description: The programme's name, such as "hrp-origin-and-commodity". Derived from the goal when nobody names one.

goal.description: One sentence: what is being built, and for whom.

repos.description: Where the programme builds: each repo key mapped to its workspace-relative folder, such as { "frontend": "repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend" }. The tests repo is always one of them. The consolidator copies it into backlog.json's `repos`, adding each GitHub slug.

reposWhy.description: One line saying why these repos, so the report can show the choice and a wrong guess is caught.

precedence.description: Every source id, from most to least authoritative. It decides conflicts: the reconciler adopts the higher-ranked source's position.

sources.description: Every source the run distils. One extract agent and one or more verify agents run per source.

text.description: Text that is not empty or only whitespace.

repoKey.description: A lower-case repo key, such as "frontend", "tests" or "insbackend".

sourceId.description: A source id: a lower-case prefix, a colon, then a name with no spaces, such as "repo:tests", "confluence:6518997274" or "ruling:sam-2026-09-29". Its file slug is the id with every character other than a letter, digit, dot or hyphen turned into a hyphen, such as "repo-tests".

source.description: One source. Its scope hash is the sha256 of its kind, locator and scope: change any of them and `tim distil status` marks the source stale, so the next launch extracts it again.

id.description: The source's id, used in precedence, in every claim's provenance and in conflict positions.

kind.description: What sort of source it is. It picks the extract brief: repo (a repo in the workspace, read for what it does today and what has been ruled), confluence (a page fetched to <workarea>/sources/<page-id>.json), web (a public page or site), document (a file under <workarea>/sources/, such as a docx, PDF, text or meeting notes), trace (a directory of Playwright trace zips, or a set already mined under workareas/trace-requirements/), ruling (a decision from the owner of the work, written up as a file under <workarea>/sources/) or image (a design or screenshot, read one at a time).

locator.description: Where the source is: a workspace-relative path (repos/..., workareas/...), a Confluence page file, or a URL for a web source.

scope.description: Which part of the source to distil, such as "whole page" or "the origin and commodity pages, spec/decisions.json". Distil a slice of a big source well rather than all of it thinly.

role.description: What the source is authoritative for, such as "what exists today and what has already been ruled" or "policy: what data must be captured".
